As could be seen from the said complaint, the allegations were three fold.

Firstly, the amount of Rupee Six Lakhs that the complainant had received as alimony was NC: 2024:KHC-D:3561 invested in a fixed deposit and her father had withdrawn the interest that was accruing on the said fixed deposit by using withdrawal slips and therefore, petitioners had cheated her.

3. The second allegation was that in the month of May 2018 a sum of Rupees One Lakh in Gayatri Pathina Sahakara Co-operative bank was encashed and in the month of August a further fixed deposit of Rupees 11,50,000/- was encashed by her at the behest of her father who had promised her to secure a job by spending Rs.15,15,000/-.
4. The third set of allegation was that her brother had forged her signature on a genealogical tree on 30.7.2018 and was therefore guilty of forging the signature.
5. On investigation, the police have laid a charge sheet.
In order to support the charge sheet, in which the following allegations were made against the petitioners:

6. As could be seen from the charges leveled against the petitioners, the essential charge against them is that they had forged the signature of the second respondent in the genealogical tree and secured the registration of a document.
Since the charge sheet does not make any allegations regarding the illegal withdrawal or against the encashment of the fixed deposit amounting to Rs.15,15,000/-.

7. Thus, the only charge that has remained after investigation was that the petitioners had forged the signature of the second respondent in a genealogical tree and had secured the registration of a Pundalik Rao T S/O. 8. Learned counsel for the petitioners places on record the genealogical tree, which is alleged to have been forged by the petitioners and the same reads as follows:

9.

As could be seen from the said affidavit, the affidavit was sworn to by the second respondent herself, in NC: 2024:KHC-D:3561 which she swore to the contents of the affidavit, which was essentially stating her family tree.
She also stated in this affidavit that she required this genealogical tree for the purpose of submitting the same to the Thasildar, Hospete for getting the katha changed in her favor.

10. It is therefore clear that this genealogical tree, even assuming it is forged, would only enure to the benefit of the second respondent and the petitioners would gain absolutely no benefit by this alleged forged genealogical tree.
Since the fundamental premise that the genealogical tree was forged in order to secure the registration of document would have to necessarily fail.
11. It is also to be noticed that this genealogical tree is not a document, which is necessary for enabling the registration of any document.
It is neither a prescribed document nor a document required by any provision of law to facilitate the registration of another document.

12. In this view of the matter, it is clear that there is absolutely no material that has been unearthed during the course of the investigation so as to maintain the charge against the petitioners and subject them to a trial and therefore, I am NC: 2024:KHC-D:3561 of the view that this is an appropriate case to quash the proceedings in order to prevent the abuse of the process of law.
The petition is accordingly allowed and the proceedings against the petitioners is quashed.
